rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Allergy and autoimmune diseases ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Allergy and autoimmune diseases** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Human Health and Diseases fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  The immune system can fail in two opposite directions. **Allergy** is an over-reaction to a harmless antigen (pollen, dust, food) — IgE-coated mast cells dump histamine. **Autoimmunity** is the loss of self-tolerance: the immune system attacks the body's own tissues (rheumatoid arthritis, Type 1 diabetes). One is an attack on something harmless; the other on something that is self.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Allergy = exaggerated IgE response to harmless antigens (pollen, dust); chemicals histamine and serotonin cause sneezing, watery eyes, rashes — name the chemicals.  ·  Trick 2: Treatment: antihistamines (cetrizine), adrenaline for anaphylaxis — the two drugs to quote.

rows.text: **Most-asked points (NEB).** (1) Define allergy and name the antibody and mediator involved (IgE, histamine). (2) Why is anaphylactic shock dangerous and which drug rescues? (3) Define autoimmunity and give two diseases with the tissue attacked. (4) Contrast allergy and autoimmunity in four points.…  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Allergy = IgE + mast cells + histamine aimed at a harmless target; autoimmunity = tolerance lost, self attacked. Both are failures of recognition, in opposite directions. **Self-check:** can you name the antibody in allergy and the destroyed cells in Type 1 diabetes?
